title: Effective prenex normalization for countable Gödel truth-value sets
formal: Editorial conjecture variant of the classification question: for every countably infinite closed \(V\subseteq[0,1]\) containing 0 and 1, does Gödel logic over V admit a computable validity-preserving translation into its prenex fragment if and only if its set of valid sentences is arithmetical?
definitions:
Fix an effectively encoded first-order language with countably many predicate and function symbols of each finite arity, without equality or Delta. Structures have nonempty domains, total domain-valued functions and V-valued predicates. Interpret bottom as 0, conjunction/disjunction as min/max, implication a⇒b as 1 if a≤b and as b otherwise, and universal/existential quantifiers as infimum/supremum. Closedness of V makes these truth values lie in V. Let Valid(V) be the set of codes of sentences with value 1 in every such structure.

A prenex sentence is a finite string of first-order quantifiers followed by a quantifier-free formula. A translation is a total Turing-computable function T on sentence codes such that T(phi) is prenex and phi∈Valid(V) iff T(phi)∈Valid(V). It may use new symbols from the fixed language and need not preserve truth values or equivalence inside each structure. There is no oracle for V. The quantifiers are: for each V, there exists a finite program T; a single uniform algorithm accepting an encoding of all such V is not required.

A set of natural numbers is arithmetical if it is definable by a first-order formula in the standard natural numbers with addition and multiplication, allowing fixed natural-number parameters but no set or real parameters. The arithmetic formula and its quantifier complexity may depend on V. This precise equivalence specializes the source’s broad countable-set classification to its stated arithmetical-characterization conjecture.
answer_criterion: Prove the displayed equivalence for every V in Lean, or provide a specified countably infinite closed V and prove that one direction fails. A logically equivalent prenex theorem is sufficient where available but is not required by this validity-only target. Failure of pointwise formula equivalence alone is not a counterexample.
context: Baaz and Gamsakhurdia distinguish logically equivalent prenex forms from effective preservation of validity. Their countable-set discussion proposes arithmetical validity as the relevant dividing condition.
why: A classification would explain when quantifier normalization remains algorithmically possible in many-valued semantics.

import_provenance.original_title: Effective prenex normalization for countable Gödel truth-value sets
import_provenance.original_statement: For which countably infinite closed truth-value sets V⊆[0,1] containing 0 and 1 is there an effective transformation taking every first-order formula to a prenex formula that is valid in G_V exactly when the original is valid? This asks for preservation of validity, rather than logical equivalence, and seeks to complete Baaz–Gamsakhurdia’s classification.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The case V={1−1/(n+1):n≥0}∪{1}, and the corresponding finite-valued cases, already admit such normalization.

context_blocks.text: Baaz and Gamsakhurdia distinguish logically equivalent prenex forms from effective preservation of validity. Their countable-set discussion proposes arithmetical validity as the relevant dividing condition.

sentences: The truth values form a countably infinite closed subset of the unit interval.
The translation must preserve validity rather than every model’s truth value.
A separate ordinary computable translation may be chosen for each truth-value set.
The selected conjecture equates existence of that translation with arithmetical validity.
This explicitly replaces the unrestricted classification request by a checkable equivalence.
